description: Single-panel line plot with vertical error bars. The ordinate is labelled "Average Grain Size (μm)" (linear scale, 0–100, major gridline ticks every 10 μm); the abscissa is labelled "Temperature (°C)" (800–1300, ticks every 100 °C, data points at 900, 950, 1000, 1100 and 1200 °C). Three series are plotted, each named by in-plot legend text adjacent to its curve: "α2 (banded shape)" as magenta diamonds, the coarsest series; "γ" as blue triangles, intermediate; and "α1 (mainly among γ grains)" as red squares, the finest. Every point carries a vertical error bar. All three curves rise with annealing temperature. α2 runs from between the 20 and 30 μm gridlines at 900 °C up to between the 60 and 70 μm gridlines at 1200 °C, and its 1200 °C error bar is the largest, spanning above the 90 μm gridline. γ rises from about the 5 μm gridline to between the 30 and 40 μm gridlines. α1 dips slightly between 900 and 950 °C before rising to just above the 20 μm gridline at 1200 °C. The figure argues that the two ferrite populations must be treated separately: banded α2 and γ coarsen strongly above 900 °C, whereas fine α1 among γ grains grows little until above 1000 °C. No numeric values are printed on the plot itself.
measured_quantities: standard deviation of average grain size (μm)

observations.observation: The plot axes are 'Average Grain Size (μm)' (0–100, ticks every 10) versus 'Temperature (°C)' (800–1300, ticks every 100 °C).
Three curves are plotted and labelled inside the panel: 'α2 (banded shape)' (magenta diamonds), 'γ' (blue triangles) and 'α1 (mainly among γ grains)' (red squares).
Data points lie at 900, 950, 1000, 1100 and 1200 °C; there is no point at 800 or 1300 °C.
The magenta α2 (banded shape) curve is the highest of the three, running from between the 20 and 30 μm gridlines at 900 °C to between the 60 and 70 μm gridlines at 1200 °C.
The blue γ curve rises from about the 5 μm gridline at 900 °C to between the 30 and 40 μm gridlines at 1200 °C.
The red α1 (mainly among γ grains) curve is the lowest; it decreases slightly between 900 and 950 °C and then rises to just above the 20 μm gridline at 1200 °C.
Every data point has a vertical error bar; the largest is on α2 at 1200 °C, extending from roughly the 45 μm gridline to above the 90 μm gridline.
The caption states the error bars represent the standard deviations.

The caption states the ferrite marked as α is split into two populations (mainly distributed among γ grains, versus continuously distributed in banded shape with large grains) because their average grain sizes differ greatly; in the supplied caption text the two symbols are printed identically as α, whereas the citing text names them α1 and α2.
The citing text states the plotted values were obtained from SEM micrographs.
The citing text states that between 900 °C and 1200 °C the average grain size of γ increases from 5.5 μm to 36.0 μm and that of α2 increases from 26.1 μm to 68.4 μm.
The citing text states the grain size of α1 decreases from 3.2 μm to 2.5 μm between 900 °C and 950 °C, then increases from 2.5 μm to 22.2 μm between 950 °C and 1200 °C.
The citing text interprets the contiguous banded α2 as mainly the ferrite that solidified first during casting, and states that banded structure becomes less contiguous at higher temperatures.

subfigures.description: Line plot of average grain size (μm, 0–100) versus annealing temperature (°C, 800–1300) with three error-barred series: magenta diamonds labelled α2 (banded shape), blue triangles labelled γ, and red squares labelled α1 (mainly among γ grains). α2 is highest and coarsest, γ intermediate, α1 lowest; all increase with temperature, with a slight dip of α1 between 900 and 950 °C.
